sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of PC and Console Video Games via Digital Stores

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Latin American codified system; commercial practice incorporates Anglo-American drafting standards)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force 2012)
Panama-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 1991)
Panama-Netherlands Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (in force 2000)
Panama-Republic of Korea Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Fundaciones de Interés Privado), reglamentada por el Decreto Ejecutivo No. 417 de 1995; Código Fiscal de la República de Panamá (territorial taxation); AML/CFT framework: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 as amended by Ley No. 70 de 6 de junio de 2019 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales ante la Dirección General de Ingresos - DGI); UAF regulations and GAFILAT/FATF standards. Initial patrimony is mandatory under Law 25 of 1995 but no statutory minimum is fixed; commercial practice adopts USD 100 as declared foundation patrimony.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - the Panamanian beneficiary owner registry is confidential, administered by the DGI, and accessible only to tax, UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero), law enforcement, and international exchange-of-information partners; no public inspection of UBO data. Private Interest Foundations maintain statutory privacy and nominee-friendly governance (founder, council, protector, beneficiaries).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport bio-data pages of all founders, Foundation Council members, and protector (if appointed)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority in the country of residence (e.g., U.S. Department of State)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by issuing country's competent authority; non-Hague jurisdictions require Consular Legalization at the Panamanian Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for incorporation (Poder General de Representación) granted by foreign founder to the Panamanian resident agent or local attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the founder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; original must be physically submitted to the notarial protocol in Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of corporate founder (if the founder is a legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry (e.g., Secretary of State of Delaware or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization through the competent authority of the jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of residential address used for source-of-funds verification and PEP/AML screening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank and/or utility company in the founder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified notarial copy plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; Spanish translation must be certified

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory under Law 23 of 2015 and GAFILAT/FATF standards: (i) PEP screening of all founders, protectors, beneficiaries, and Foundation Council members, including 12-month cooling-off for former PEPs and their close associates; (ii) continuous screening against OFAC SDN, UN Consolidated, EU, UK HMT, and Panamanian UAF lists, with particular attention to Steam/PlayStation US-dollar settlement flows; (iii) risk-based CDD/EDD with documented source-of-funds evidence for game-publishing revenues; (iv) resident agent obligation to file suspicious transaction reports (ROS) with the UAF within 24 hours of suspicion; (v) UBO declaration to the DGI registry upon formation and within 15 days of any material change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Portal de Servicios en Línea (official website: https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa; electronic name reservation module denominated 'Certificado de Búsqueda y Reserva de Nombre')
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All constitutional documents are drafted in Spanish. The foundation name must contain the statutory descriptor 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or the abbreviation 'F.I.P.' as a mandatory tagline. The distinctive part of the name may be in Spanish or any Latin-script language; non-Roman scripts (CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be phonetically transliterated into Latin characters. Accents and diacritical marks are normalized by the registry; only alphanumeric characters and limited punctuation are accepted.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Bank, Banca, Financiera, Crédito, Fideicomiso, Trust (requires Superintendencia de Bancos approval)
Seguros, Reaseguros, Aseguradora, Previsora (requires Superintendencia de Seguros approval)
Gobierno, Nacional, Oficial, Ministerio, Estatal, Municipal, Policía, Cruz Roja, UNESCO (state and international organizational identifiers)
Casino, Juego, Lotería, Apuestas, Casa de Apuestas (gambling-related tokens trigger gaming licensing review, incompatible with a standard game-publishing PIF)
Compañía, Corporation, Inc., Corp., Limited, Ltd., S.A. (corporate suffixes incompatible with Private Interest Foundation legal form)
Panamá, Panama (restricted if it implies official government designation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant's registered attorney may file a 'recurso de reconsideración' within 3 business days before the Dirección General del Registro Público, followed by a 'recurso de apelación' within 5 business days before the Director General (final administrative instance), pursuant to Ley No. 38 de 2000. In parallel, counsel should resubmit an online name reservation with a modified distinctive element (add initials, secondary word, or distinctive suffix) to avoid phonetically identical or confusingly similar collisions. The registry's phonetic search covers homonymy, so a trademark clearance letter is recommended when the gaming brand coexists with existing trademarks.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted - the PIF must maintain a registered office in Panama at the resident agent's physical address; day-to-day Steam/PlayStation publishing operations can be managed entirely remotely. The PIF should not develop Panamanian-source selling, marketing, or physical presence activities in order to preserve territorial-source tax neutrality; contracting with Valve/PlayStation storefronts as a non-resident publisher is the recommended substance model.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - below 5% annualized probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection. The Registro Público does not routinely inspect; DGI and UAF audit activity is concentrated in financial services and high-risk construction sectors. The resident agent must nevertheless maintain at the registered office: foundation charter, by-laws, Foundation Council minutes, register of beneficiaries, and the UBO declaration file, sufficient to withstand any documentary verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended by Law 49 of 2012 and Law 11 of 2015; Articles 1-22 (creation, registration, and governance of Foundations of Private Interest).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Private Interest Foundation Section.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva / Escritura de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Panamanian law requires a minimum initial foundation capital of USD 10,000. This capital may be contributed in cash, securities, or tangible assets, and it may be partially unpaid at formation. No escrow or bank deposit requirement is imposed at registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The subscription of the initial capital of USD 10,000 is accepted and fully recorded in the Foundation accounts. (2) The registered office is adopted at the address stated in the Foundation Charter, Panama City, Republic of Panama. (3) The following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each vested with the powers specified in the Foundation Charter and Regulations. (4) The Foundation Regulations are approved, and the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, engage professional advisors, and perform all acts necessary for the digital publishing business. This resolution is effective immediately and recorded in the Foundation minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Name Section (Registro Público de Panamá, Departamento de Nombres).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request through the Public Registry's online portal or in-person window. Provide two preferred names for the Private Interest Foundation. Pay the search fee. Upon approval, the name is reserved for the applicant for a non-extendable period of 30 days.
required_dossiers: Copy of applicant ID or passport
Power of attorney if filed through representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is unavailable or rejected, file a new name search request with alternative names. No cure request is permitted; the applicant must submit up to two substitute names within the same business day if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting the Foundation Charter and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in Panama or a Panamanian licensed attorney.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter in Spanish (or bilingual English/Spanish), including foundation name, purpose, initial capital, founder, foundation council members, registered agent, registered office, and beneficiary provisions. The internal Regulations may be separate and are not publicly registered.
required_dossiers: Identification of founder and initial Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Public Registry or notary queries charter wording, revise the affected clause and submit a corrected draft within 10 business days. No fine applies if corrected before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama City or provincial notaries.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a Panamanian notary or execute the Foundation Charter before a foreign notary with apostille, followed by submission to a Panamanian notary for formalization. The notary authenticates signatures and the certificate of the Registered Agent.
required_dossiers: Government-issued identification of all signing parties
Certificate of apostille if signed abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects incomplete signatures or missing annexes, the parties must promptly execute corrected signature pages; the notarial fee may be reduced or waived at the notary's discretion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundation Section (Registro de Fundaciones de Interés Privado).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Foundation Charter with the Public Registry along with the official registration application. Pay the government filing fee. The Registry examines the document for statutory compliance and issues the registration certificate (Certificado de Registro).
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter (original and two certified copies)
Proof of payment of registration fees
Power of attorney if filed through a legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect notice (nota de defecto), the applicant must cure the defect within the statutory period by filing a corrective amendment or supplemental document; resubmission fee of USD 25 applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Registered Office and Registered Agent Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama and authorized Registered Agent in Panama.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registered Agent must confirm in writing the maintenance of a registered office at a Panamanian physical address. The Foundation receives an official tax identification number (RUC) and a certificate of registered agent appointment from the Registry.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate from the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office address is invalid or the registered agent resigns, the Foundation must appoint a new registered agent within 15 days by filing an amendment in the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Directorate of Revenue (DGI) of the Panama Ministry of Economy and Finance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a taxpayer identification number (RUC) and, if the Foundation will be considered a taxable entity, register for income tax and any applicable annual license. Digital publishing activity is generally outside Panamanian territorial tax scope, but a formal registration is prudent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC application is delayed, submit an expedited request to the DGI local office and obtain a provisional receipt number to proceed with banking and Steam/PlayStation payout contracts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing authority is mandated for digital software publishing; voluntary registration is available with the Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) for export promotion.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating permit required under Panamanian law for pure digital publishing; an Aviso de Operación may be obtained from MICI if a physical commercial office is maintained.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – software publishing involves no physical industrial plant, manufacturing, or pollutant discharge; no EIA filing is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for the core digital publishing activity. If a future physical office lease is established, comply with municipal solid waste disposal standards, electrical safety codes, and any building-related sanitation requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for the digital publishing activity. If an office or workspace is established, obtain a fire safety inspection certificate from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá and adhere to workplace safety requirements under MITRADEL (Ministry of Labor and Manpower Development).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); official e-portal: 'Sede Electrónica' at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (plus DGI front-desk 'Módulo de Atención al Contribuyente' at Plaza Fortaleza, Avenida 12 de Octubre, Panama City); the Registro Público de Panamá serves as the corporate registry issuing the foundation registration certificate required for tax enrolment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Constitute the Private Interest Foundation (Fundación de Interés Privado, Law 25 of 1995) by public deed, appoint the Consejo de Fundación and the resident attorney (Abogado Idóneo), and register at the Registro Público; Step 2: obtain the Registro Público certificate (Copia Simple/Personería Jurídica) and the foundation by-laws (Reglamento); Step 3: file the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) application through DGI Sede Electrónica using Form Solicitud/RUC, attaching the deed, Public Registry certificate, appointment minutes, passports/IDs of the Foundation Council members and resident agent, and a sworn declaration of the principal place of management and the 'causa fuente'; Step 4: if the PIF will invoice Panamanian-source or exported services, file the Aviso de Operación (Notice of Operation) and elect the value-added tax status as 'causante de ITBMS'; Step 5: request enrolment in the DGI Módulo de Exportador de Servicios (services-exporter registration module) to enable zero-rated ITBMS invoicing; the RUC is issued immediately-approximate the same business day for normal applications (with a physical inspection only if the PIF maintains a registered local office).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope (PIF tax-transparent or Hybrid: income tax follows the territorial source criterion; Panamanian-source income is assessable on the foundation at the 25% general corporate rate (non-resident digital publishing income attributed to the PIF, sourced abroad, is outside Panama's tax net); the foundation is exempt from income tax on foreign-source assets and distributions; the annual 'Bono de Fundación' of USD 300 is payable to the MEF each year without a tax return requirement where no Panamanian-source income arises)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a US-style check-the-box entity-classification election. Available statutory elections and options: (i) exporter option between ITBMS input credit vs. direct refund (Código Fiscal, Art. 1050-F); (ii) the 'acreditamiento' choice for ITBMS paid on purchases used in exported services; (iii) registration option for the special 'proveedor de servicios digitales' regime under Law 254 of 2021 (Régimen de Digital) to use simplified collection mechanics; (iv) option to keep books in conformity with NIIF vs. local statutory accounting via the DGI 'Máxima' journal?; and (v) written election to compute depreciation and carryfoward NOLs under the standard statutory rules, with no hybrid-mismatch or transparent-entity election available for PIFs.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — Full banking and foreign exchange administration authority; the Republic of Panama has no issuing central bank under the 1904 Monetary Agreement with the United States; the U.S. Dollar is the official legal tender pursuant to the National Constitution and Decree Law No. 9 of 1970, and Banco Nacional de Panamá acts solely as the fiscal agent of the State.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full dollarization ensures absolute currency convertibility for both capital and current account transactions. Panama maintains no exchange control restrictions on the transfer of dividends, royalties, licensing fees, or profit remittances originating from the commercial activities of a Private Interest Foundation (PIF). Cross-border repatriation is unrestricted and requires no prior authorization from any monetary authority; the only operative gate is the anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing (AML/CFT) verification regime under Law 23 of 2015, including the filing of mandatory currency and suspicious transaction reports where thresholds apply. Profit remittances from a PIF engaged in digital publishing are treated as ordinary commercial transfers and are free from foreign exchange approval, conversion, or surrender obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panamanian law imposes no statutory timeline, percentage, or escrow requirement for the surrender of export proceeds. All proceeds from digital publishing sales, Steam/Valve payouts, PlayStation Store settlements, and other software licensing revenue may be retained in U.S. Dollars within domestic or offshore accounts without exchange notification or mandatory conversion. The PIF must nonetheless maintain documentary evidence of each commercial receipt, including platform-generated settlement statements and the underlying Steamworks / PlayStation Partner agreements, to demonstrate the lawful origin of funds for banking due diligence and tax transparency purposes. No surrender rule exists because the functional and reporting currency of Panama is the U.S. Dollar.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Operational Account / Treasury Settlement Account
USD Corporate Operational Account and Treasury Sweep
USD Merchant and Operational Clearing Account
USD Corporate Non-Resident Account / Escrow for PIF
USD Operating and Foreign Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium as the primary treasury rail; foreign digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and non-resident fintech licensees have no passporting rights into Panama and cannot open domestic settlement accounts in the name of a Panamanian PIF. Digital payment services operating in Panama must be authorized by the SBP under the applicable payment-services regulatory framework, which generally requires a local presence and a licensed bank or trust partner. Global EMIs such as Wise, Nium, or Stripe can be used only as alternative collection or disbursement interfaces where payouts are ultimately cleared through an SBP-licensed correspondent institution; they are not substitutes for a regulated Panamanian bank account. The PIF should maintain a Tier-1 domestic bank account as the single point of truth for liquidity, foreign exchange, and compliance reporting, with fintech rails limited to non-settlement data exchange and reconciliation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance is generally mandated for the initial onboarding of a Private Interest Foundation. At least one member of the Foundation Council (or the authorized registered agent with sufficient written power) must appear physically before the bank's compliance officer and a Panamanian notary public for identity verification, signature specimen, and biometric capture. Remote opening is possible only under the internal discretion of privately owned banks for subsequent signatories or for pre-existing clients with a comprehensive relationship history. SBP regulations require enhanced due diligence for all non-resident and opaque structures, including PIFs; the bank will reject applications in which the foundation regulations do not clearly identify the protectors, final beneficiaries, and economic substance framework.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived opacity of the PIF structure: the private Registry of Panama does not publicly disclose beneficiaries, and banks universally demand complete transparency over the foundation charter and council resolutions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled founding act and foundation regulations; formal council resolution appointing the banking signatories; bank-grade beneficial ownership register completed in strict compliance with Law 23 of 2015; registered agent professional comfort letter addressing the purpose and commercial substance of the PIF.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or unsupported source of funds and source of wealth for the initial foundation endowment and subsequent platform payouts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three years of bank statements of the benefactor; certified copy of the endowment transfer instruments; signed source-of-wealth questionnaire; audited or reviewed financial statements; tax residence certificates and tax returns of the donor; platform settlement history demonstrating that all Steam and PlayStation receipts derive from recognized digital-store transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, cross-border digital receipts without physical contracts or verifiable trade invoices, which may be misclassified as unreported commercial activity or illicit gaming-related proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Steamworks Distribution Agreement and/or PlayStation Partner Agreement; platform-generated merchant settlement statements; registered intellectual property certificates (trademarks, copyrights); licensing and royalty schedule; annual reconciliation between platform net-revenue reports and bank account credits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or adverse-media exposure involving counterparties, including platform entities, co-publishers, or payment service providers in the video game distribution chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC, EU, UN, and equivalent sanctions screening results for all principal parties, signatories, and intermediate clearing agents; beneficial owner screening certificates; negative news reports and compliance vendor searches; corporate registry extracts confirming no connection to sanctioned jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of unregulated crypto-asset or peer-to-peer cash-out rails for converting Steam wallet balances or international sales proceeds into fiat currency, which is an automatic red flag for Panamanian banks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate treasury policy explicitly prohibiting crypto settlement; annual CFO or foundation council declaration that all proceeds are received exclusively via regulated SWIFT, Fedwire, or ACH rails; platform payout settings evidencing direct credit to the declared SBP-licensed bank account; no references to crypto addresses or unregulated intermediaries in bank narratives.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections and platform remittances to the PIF's Panamanian account must be routed via the SWIFT network (MT103) or through the U.S. Fedwire/CHIPS clearing system for same-day USD settlement, as Panama's banking system clears USD by correspondent relationship with U.S. banks. The wire narrative must precisely state the economic purpose, such as 'Steamworks Royalties under Agreement No. XXX' or 'PlayStation Store Publishing Revenue' accompanied by the relevant platform settlement reference number. Since Panama is fully dollarized, no foreign-exchange authorization or purpose-code registration is required by the central bank; however, the receiving bank's AML operation will classify the inbound transfer under the customer's declared commercial profile. Verification documentation must be retained for each inbound credit: platform payout receipts, invoice copies, and digital-store sales dashboards to ensure audit- and tax-ready traceability of every capital entry.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for a digital publishing PIF are executed primarily as corporate wire transfers (SWIFT MT103) via the PIF's SBP-licensed bank to licensors, co-publishers, contractors, and tax authorities. For physical console merchandise or co-production obligations, a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) may be opened by the Panamanian bank, with documents comprising bill of lading, commercial invoice, certificate of origin, and conformity certificate. Recurring portal payments, such as monthly developer royalties or store-level contributions from the Steam and PlayStation ecosystems, are settled on open-account terms through SWIFT or ACH batches supported by platform-generated clearing statements. USD-denominated disbursements may clear directly through US correspondents without conversion; EUR/GBP disbursements are converted by the domestic bank at the current wholesale exchange rate with full transfer documentation to satisfy transfer-pricing and economic-substance standards for the base territory.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright U.S. Dollar / Euro (USD/EUR) and U.S. Dollar / British Pound (USD/GBP) foreign exchange forwards transacted with SBP-licensed domestic banks or their international correspondents

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on Latin American emerging-market currencies (e.g., USD/BRL, USD/CLP, USD/MXN) applicable when Steam and PlayStation local-currency sales are periodically consolidated and converted to USD
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR and USD/GBP) for matched funding of development advances and license prepayments
European-style and exotic FX options for multi-year publishing pipelines with tranched royalty milestones
FX swaps within the same clearing bank to cover temporary liquidity mismatches between platform payout cycles and operating disbursement dates
Interest rate and cross-currency basis swaps for fixed-rate funding structures linked to a future distribution or catalogue acquisition

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foundation tax (tasa única anual) for Private Interest Foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year; payment is accepted during 1 January – 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 10% late-payment surcharge on the USD 300 fee plus statutory interest computed from the day after the due date; prolonged non-payment can lead to suspension of tax-clearance certificates and administrative strike-off action by the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation (declaración anual de beneficiario final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI Beneficial-Owner Registry established under Law 70 of 2019
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 calendar days after the anniversary of the initial beneficial-owner registration or on the DGI-published confirmation date; changes in beneficial ownership are reportable within 15 calendar days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for late, false, or incomplete filings; the foundation may be blocked from obtaining tax-clearance or good-standing certificates until the beneficial-owner information is ratified.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income-tax return (declaración de renta) where Panama-source taxable income exists
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the foundation's fiscal year-end; for calendar-year accounts, due on or before 31 March of the following year. No income-tax return is required where all digital-store publishing receipts are exclusively foreign-source.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory interest on unpaid tax, late-filing fines, and fines up to the amount of omitted tax for incorrect declarations; repeated failure to file may suspend the foundation's tax ID and trigger enforced collection.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is required when the foundation's Panama-source annual gross revenue reaches or exceeds USD 1,000,000, or when expressly required by the foundation charter, the foundation council, a beneficiary, or the DGI. A Private Interest Foundation deriving only foreign software and console sales is not statutorily obliged to file audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama for entities requiring statutory financial statements; Panamanian local GAAP (NIF / IFRS for SMEs) is acceptable where no audit is mandatory. Books may be kept in Spanish or English and must accurately reflect the foundation's transactions and financial position.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 70 of 2019 and its implementing rules, the Private Interest Foundation must disclose and annually ratify its beneficial owners through the DGI Beneficial-Owner Registry. The registry captures the founder, foundation council members, and beneficiaries with identifiable foundation rights. Any transfer of beneficial interests or foundation rights must be reported within 15 calendar days, and the annual confirmation must be filed even when no ownership change has occurred during the year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and Classes of Foundation Interests

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required for a foreign-source PIF; if a voluntary or triggered audit is commissioned, US$2,500 – US$5,000 in Panama City

stage_6.entry_description: Taxpayer Identification Number (Registro Único de Contribuyente) and check digit.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PIF must first obtain a RUC through the ATTT registration process for non-resident entities.
